title: A comprehensive psychometrics of cognitive ability measures: Reliability, practice effects, and the stability of latent factor structures across retesting
authors: Matthew K. Robison, Stephen Campbell, Lauren D. Garner, Ciara Sibley, Joseph Coyne
caption_short: Schematic of the three verbal memory tasks of the battery: word recognition (20 studied words, then 10 old and 10 new test words), cued recall of 10 word pairs, and immediate free recall of 10-word lists; each task done twice about two weeks apart.
notes: Drawn by us: the paper (CC BY 4.0, open access, PMC12855318) has six figures and all of them are factor-analysis diagrams or scatterplots (Fig. 1-2 confirmatory factor analyses, Fig. 3 factor scores across attempts, Fig. 4 latent state-trait model, Fig. 5-6 drift-rate factor models); none shows a task. Task details in the schematic are from the paper's Method section (full text via Europe PMC JATS XML): recognition - 5 lists of 20 six-letter words, 3 s each with a 1 s mask, test of 20 words (10 old, 10 new) with F = old and J = new, 5 s limit; cued recall - 10 lists of 10 unrelated four-letter word pairs, 3 s each with a 1 s mask, cue words in a random order, 5 s to type the target, example FROG-CAPE; immediate free recall - 10 lists of 10 five-letter words, 3 s each with a 1 s mask, typed recall in any order. 'Each measure was completed twice, separated by a period of 2 weeks' (abstract). Example words other than FROG-CAPE are made up (garden, silver, pencil, rocket are six letters; LAMP-SOFA four; chair, bread five). The practice lists in the data (list 0) are not drawn. Rendered with Pillow (DejaVu Sans). Our data come from the Rouder lab data0 repository (controlBatteries/Robison2026), which matches this study (same 24-task battery and memory tasks, two attempts, about 270 participant ids); the paper's own data link is osf.io/j4tzh.
